# DSH Lock Screen
English | 中文

A full-screen password lock for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`).
Running long tasks? Lock the UI before you

walk away, and nobody passing your desk sees a session, a
tool call, a file path or an API key spel

body passing your desk sees a session, a
tool call, a file path or an API key spelled out in a diff.
The lock is **purely visual**. The agent keeps running in the Host process the whole time — the plug

in
never touches sessions, timers, streams or the sandbox. It does not even have a handle to them.
## Features
- **One click or one shortcut.** A lock button at the sidebar foot, and `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + L` from

anywhere.
- **Password gate.** Salted SHA-256 in `localStorage`; the plaintext never leaves the pass

word field.
- **Survives a reload.** The locked state is persisted, so refreshing the page, reopenin

g the window or
restarting DSH still shows the lock — not the session behind it. Multiple tabs sync

through `storage` events.
- **Password optional.** You can lock without a password (unlock = one cli

ck on a screen only you asked for),
or remove the password later from the same panel.
- **Brute-forc

e brakes.** Three wrong attempts start a cooldown (5 s, doubling, capped at 60 s) with a live
countd

own; input and button stay disabled until it expires.
- **Hides the title too.** The page title beco

mes `DSH (locked)` while locked, and is restored on unlock.
- **Follows the theme.** Light and dark,

using only Harness `--dsw-alias-*` tokens (surfaces derived with
`color-mix`), so it does not fight

a custom theme.
- **No dependencies, no network, no files.** One client module, no build step, noth
ing installed at runtime.

From the DSH plugin manager (recommended — the desktop app's **Settings → Plugins**, or the
`dshmark
et` market once this plugin is listed):

From a checkout of this repo:

After installing, **refresh the Web UI once** (the client module loads at page load). The lock butto

n
appears at the bottom of the sidebar, next to Settings.
## Use
| Action | How |

| Lock now | Click the lock at the sidebar foot, or press `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + L` |
| Unlock | Type t

he password and press `Enter` |
| Set / change / remove the password | `Shift` + click the lock (ope

ns the panel without locking) |
| Lock without a password | Third row of the setup panel: “Lock with

out locking) |
| Lock without a password | Third row of the setup panel: “Lock without a password” |
The first time you click the lock, the setup panel asks for a password (at least 4 characters, twice

).
Saving it locks immediately.
## What it is not
This is a **privacy screen, not a security boundary**:
- It stops the person who walks past your desk from reading the screen. It does not stop someone who

can
operate the machine — Task Manager, the file manager, another browser, or `localStorage` itself

are all
outside its reach.
- The password is stored as a salted hash in this profile's `localStorag

e`
(keys `dsh.lock-screen.credential`, `dsh.lock-screen.locked`). It is not encryption, and there is

no
recovery path: forget it and you clear those two keys (DevTools console) or remove the plugin.
-
Background tasks are deliberately unaffected. That is the point: you come back to finished work.
If you need real isolation, use the OS lock screen or a separate OS account.
## How it works
Two slots, one module:
- `sidebar.footer.action` — the lock button (`order: 10`), icon-only when the sidebar is collapsed t

o a rail.
- `shell.overlay` — the full-screen layer (`order: 100`) holding the lock screen and the s
`shell.overlay` — the full-screen layer (`order: 100`) holding the lock screen and the setup panel.
`client.js` is a single ES module registered through `window.__ModuleLoader__.load(...)`, written wi

th
`React.createElement` (no JSX, no bundler). It injects exactly two services, `slots` and `locale`

, and
registers both slots inside `ctx.effect` so they are removed on unload. UI strings live in
`lo

cale/en.json` / `locale/zh.json` and are read through the locale service, so the panel follows the
H

`locale/zh.json` and are read through the locale service, so the panel follows the
Harness language.
State is a small module-level store (`useSyncExternalStore`) persisted to `localStorage`:
| Key | Value |

| `dsh.lock-screen.locked` | `"1"` / `"0"` |
| `dsh.lock-screen.credential` | `{"v":1,"salt":"<hex>"

locked` | `"1"` / `"0"` |
| `dsh.lock-screen.credential` | `{"v":1,"salt":"<hex>","hash":"<hex>"}` |
`hash = SHA-256(salt + password)` via WebCrypto; a small fallback keeps it working on hosts without

salt + password)` via WebCrypto; a small fallback keeps it working on hosts without
`crypto.subtle`.
While locked, a capture-phase `keydown` handler swallows shortcuts outside the overlay and keeps `Ta

b`
inside the password field, so the app behind the layer does not react to a bystander's typing.
## Development

There is no build step. To iterate on the UI without installing, open
`docs/harness.html` — it loads

React from a CDN, fakes the two services,
imports the real `client.js` and renders both slots next

to a stub conversation list. It also has a small
HUD to flip light/dark and reset the stored passwor

a stub conversation list. It also has a small
HUD to flip light/dark and reset the stored password.
Because the module is loaded through the plugin manager's symlinked copy, an edit under this folder

is
live **after a page refresh** in a running GUI.
## Compatibility

- DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.4` (Web UI, desktop app included).
- Verified on DSH Desktop `2.0.21-next` / `dsh

0.2.1-rc.4`, light and dark.
- Languages: English, 简体中文.
